messages:
Jada Williams: we need to lock down audit logging requirements for auto actions (pause/rollback/suppress). trying to avoid re-litigating later when console UI wants “why did it rollback?”

Felix Schneider: +1. Console wants a timeline entry that’s explainable, and also something we can point incident retros at. What’s the minimum schema we can standardize on?

Kevin Osei: from compliance side: need to be able to answer “who/what changed customer traffic and why”, and prove it wasn’t arbitrary. Also need integrity + retention expectations (SOC2-ish). Prefer immutable event stream.

Ethan Park: reminder: controller is acting service most of the time, but we’ll also have admin override endpoints. So actor needs to support both “system” and “human”.

Benji Okafor: policy engine will version policies. We should include `policy_id` + `policy_version` (or hash) used at decision time. Also include effective defaults vs override (per-rollout).

Allison Grant: observability standard note: avoid dumping huge metric blobs into audit logs. Link to snapshot/dash instead.

Sean Gallagher: + the incident use case is “show me what monitor fired, on what window, with what sample size / staleness.” We’ll get paged on this. Need enough to debug false positives.

Rafael Mendes: runbook needs to say “check monitor freshness + sample gating was met.” If the audit event has fields for that, it’s way easier.

Jada Williams: ok fields I’m thinking (rough):
- event_type: ROLLOUT_AUTO_ACTION_DECISION / ROLLOUT_AUTO_ACTION_EXECUTION
- decision: pause|rollback|shift_to_baseline|suppress|no_action
- reason: slo_breach|monitor_stale|min_samples_not_met|incident_override|admin_override|policy_disabled
- rollout_id, rollout_step_id, rollout_step_name
- scope: service, route, model, model_version, region, customer_tier
- monitors: monitor_ids (?)
- evaluation: windows (fast/slow), burn_rate, error_budget_remaining?
- metrics snapshot ref
- correlation ids
Thoughts?

Felix Schneider: +1. Also need `baseline_model_version` and `candidate_model_version` at time of decision. UI needs to show “rolled back from X -> Y”.

Chloe Martin: for A/B: also traffic split before/after would be useful (like 90/10 -> 100/0). Maybe keep as a small string field, not a giant object.

Kevin Osei: on “metrics snapshot ref”: ok, but the audit event should still store enough to be meaningful years later. At least the monitor name + provider + query key. If the dashboard changes, links rot.

Logan Wright: for event stream, we can include:
- `monitor_provider` (slo-toolkit)
- `monitor_ref` as canonical ID (string)
- `monitor_scope_key` (string) which encodes the label set we queried (route/model/region/tier)
And a `metrics_snapshot_url` (Grafana shortlink) + `metrics_snapshot_id` (internal)

Allison Grant: careful with cardinality if we include raw label sets. But for audit events it’s not Prometheus metrics, so less scary. Still: avoid including full request IDs / prompt content.

Sean Gallagher: we should explicitly state “no customer content, no prompts, no headers” in audit logs. Just rollout/control plane metadata.

Kevin Osei: yes. Also: PII. Don’t log user emails except for admin overrides (and even then, internal employee identity is fine, but still treat it as personal data). Use `actor_user_id` and a display name if needed.

Ethan Park: for admin override: want justification recorded. So `override_reason` (freeform string) but with max length. Also `override_ticket` (Jira/Linear link) if provided.

Benji Okafor: policy engine side: add `policy_source` = default_template|service_override|rollout_override and `policy_revision_id`. Helps explain when people say “why did this rollout use the aggressive template?”

Jada Williams: question: do we need a single event that includes both decision + execution result? Or separate so we can show retries / partial failures.

Rafael Mendes: separate pls. Execution can fail (e.g., policy ok but executor timed out). In incident we need to see that attempt + the eventual state.

Felix Schneider: UI can show “Decision: rollback” followed by “Execution: rollback started/complete/failed” with timestamps.

Logan Wright: makes idempotency easier too. Execution event includes `attempt_id` + `idempotency_key`.

Chloe Martin: also include `controller_instance`/`release_version` for tracing. We’ve had bugs where only one pod was misbehaving.

Kevin Osei: retention: what are we thinking? For audit events affecting traffic, 1 year minimum, ideally 18–24 months. And make sure access is restricted (RBAC).

Allison Grant: +1. We should document retention + access group. SRE oncall needs read access.

Sean Gallagher: can we also include `suppression_status` when decision is “no_action”? Like “not evaluated due to suppression window active”. Otherwise oncall sees no rollback and wonders why.

Jada Williams: yup. `suppression_reason` + `suppression_until` (timestamp) maybe.

Benji Okafor: `suppression_until` is good. Also `incident_override_id` if we have a global “don’t rollback during incident INC-xxx” flag.

Ethan Park: for “do not rollback during known incident” we should record:
- `incident_id` (PagerDuty / internal)
- who set it (actor)
- when

Felix Schneider: link to draft ADR I started: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-0128+Rollout+audit+trail+schema+for+auto+actions (WIP). I captured required fields but haven’t added privacy constraints yet.

Kevin Osei: I’ll add a section in the ADR: “Prohibited data classes” + “Retention/access”. Also note whether audit events are exportable (some customers will ask eventually).

Allison Grant: pls add note: metrics snapshot should be a reference, not raw time series. If we do include any numbers, keep it to a tiny summary:
- observed p95/p99
- observed error_rate
- sample_size
- monitor_freshness_age

Sean Gallagher: + include the burn-rate results for each window. Eg `fast_window_burn_rate=12.3`, `slow_window_burn_rate=3.1`, and the thresholds that were compared.

Jada Williams: ok. I’ll update the schema proposal accordingly:
- decision event includes summarized numbers + thresholds
- execution event includes before/after state + result

Chloe Martin: for scopes, can we standardize the string format? Like `scope_key="svc=chat-api route=/v1/chat model=llama3.1-70b ver=2026-02-04 region=us-east tier=dedicated"`.

Logan Wright: we can do `scope_key` as a stable string and also include individual fields. Helps searchability.

Kevin Osei: last ask: include `change_impact` classification (customer_impacting=true/false). This is traffic shifting so almost always true, but for internal/staging it might be false.

Rafael Mendes: + environment: prod/staging/dev.

Jada Williams: cool. Action items:
1) Felix updates ADR draft with revised field list + examples
2) Kevin adds compliance/privacy/retention section
3) I’ll make sure PR-28435 emits decision + execution events with this schema behind the feature flag

Felix Schneider: :thumbsup: I’ll push an update EOD and tag folks for review.

Kevin Osei: :thumbsup: will comment on the ADR once it’s updated.

Sean Gallagher: thanks. Once ADR lands I’ll pull pieces into the oncall runbook so it matches the actual fields.

Allison Grant: please also ping me when the schema is final so I can align naming in the metrics/doc (avoid “decision_reason” vs “reason_code” drift).

Jada Williams: will do. closing loop here once ADR is in “proposed” state.
